svg.title: NB-IoT sync: NPSS correlation and NSSS cell search
svg.text: Finding the beat (NPSS) and reading the name tag (NSSS)
A · My NPSS correlator output, 50 ms of the live signal (sketch of what the metric does)
metric
lock threshold = ¼ of the first peak (≈ 0.24)
0 ms
10 ms
20 ms
30 ms
40 ms
50 ms
one spike per 10 ms frame, always in subframe 5 → I know where every frame starts, to within one sample (0.5 µs)
B · What the NPSS is: the same 11 numbers in 11 symbols
symbol
cover
k=11 empty
Zadoff-Chu,
root 5
d(n) = exp(−jπ·5·n(n+1)/11), n = 0…10, in subframe 5
symbols 3–13, flipped by the ± cover code.
Every NB-IoT cell on Earth sends exactly this.
It tells me "a frame starts here", not who is talking.
C · Who is talking? I test all 504 cell IDs against the NSSS
PCI 260: 11.0 × the median
cell ID (PCI) hypothesis, each tried at 4 frame positions (θ = 0, ¼, ½, ¾)
NSSS for PCI 260: Zadoff-Chu root u = 260 mod 126 + 3 = 11 (length 131),
times a ± pattern: q = ⌊260 / 126⌋ = 2 → Hadamard row 63 of 128,
times a phase ramp θ that changes every 2 frames (4 values, repeating every 80 ms).
It sits in subframe 9 of even frames: 132 numbers on 11 symbols × 12 subcarriers.
Bars are a sketch of the shape; the 11.0× peak and the PCI are from my log.
